name: Yusuf Walsh

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a usual shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and lead the afternoon calls and chats at the contact centre. I have a two-year college diploma and can usually find why a refund did not arrive when other agents are stuck. I am among the strongest here, but the wage is low for leading a shift. I do not use AI tools; I want to read the payment record before I tell a customer what happened.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Dina, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. She works part time in a care home, and we have less than one month of expenses saved. There are few similar jobs nearby. I enjoy giving a new agent the right question to ask; I dread the end of a shift when I know a refund is still unresolved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my afternoon team AI Plateau leaves the phones with us, even if a note appears faster. I would still make the agent check the refund record before closing the case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my lead place is safe enough, but Dina’s care-home hours vary and we have less than a month saved. I cannot call our mortgage safe because a tool does little.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking hard refund calls and checking the account myself. In the first year of this small change, I’d stop buying a hot lunch on two afternoon shifts each week and put that money aside for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the bills, not about a small tool. A refund can be one line below where a short note stops looking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the trainee miss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yesterday a trainee thought a refund had been paid because the request was marked complete. I showed him the payment line was empty and kept the call open until we found the real date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you cut at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Dina (my partner) and I would pack food on those two shifts. We are not cutting the children’s school meals to make a new app look useful.

say: I’d say **phone work remains** with agents.
I’d insist on checking **refund payment lines** before closing a case.
think: I think my **lead place** remains in this picture.
I still fear **variable care-home hours** with thin savings.
do: Keep **hard refund calls** and account checks in 2026.
Pack **two weekly lunches** and transfer their cost toward the mortgage during the first year.
S0.quote: A refund can be one line below where a short note stops looking.
fieldNote: His **mortgage worry** predates major AI change because Dina’s care-home hours vary and savings are thin.
He caught a **request marked complete** before payment arrived.
The **lunch saving** avoids cuts to children’s essentials.

steps.text: Keep leading hard refund calls and checking payment lines
Save the cost of two weekly bought lunches toward the mortgage
Pack lunch on two afternoon shifts weekly; protect children's school meals

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take routine refund questions first, and a lead should still be paid to hear the cases that come back wrong. I would ask management how many paid afternoon seats remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could keep the difficult calls, but the centre may decide one lead can cover two teams. Dina’s part-time pay cannot meet the mortgage alone, and there are few other centres to try.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d record the refunds my team reopens and ask for the paid-hour plan. In the first year simple chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid complaint role nearby only if its written wage and hours cover our mortgage; I’d keep my current shift until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with a sick feeling when I picture an empty seat. Being good at a job does not decide how many people a company pays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What hour figure would you seek?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for afternoon paid hours, not the total number of customer messages. A smaller team could handle more angry calls without getting more pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you train on the new system?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would attend a required demonstration during paid time, but I would not spend evenings learning a system without a posted job. I have enough unknowns around the mortgage.

say: I’d ask for **paid afternoon seats** after routine chats move.
I’d defend a **paid human appeal** for wrong refunds.
think: I think my **difficult-call skill** may keep me employed.
I fear one lead could cover **two teams**, cutting my hours.
do: Record **reopened refunds**, request paid hours and attend any required demonstration only during paid time.
Seek **posted complaint work** with written mortgage-covering wage and hours in the first year.
Keep **current paid shift** until a complaint offer is signed.
S1.quote: Being good at a job does not decide how many people a company pays.
fieldNote: His **difficult-call skill** may preserve employment but not a full afternoon lead rota.
He wants **shift-specific pay**, not message counts.

steps.text: Log reopened refunds, request afternoon paid hours and attend required demonstrations only on paid time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could do the calls and even the checking I pride myself on. I would ask for a written staffing date and the names of paid jobs that remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could take my lead headset work in 2028. Robots around 2031 are later, so they do not buy us time; less than a month saved makes a mortgage gap frighteningly close.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d stop plans to replace our sound kitchen table and put any extra pay toward the next mortgage bill. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid reception job only if the written wage and hours cover the mortgage, and take a funded course during paid time only if that role requires it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. The mortgage is due before a robot can enter our contact centre.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Dina?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Dina (my partner) the old table will do. We can repair one leg and keep the replacement money for the house.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would a course be worth it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to see the posted job, its weekly hours and who pays the course time. If the company offers only a certificate, I will keep looking for wages.

say: I’d demand a **written staffing date** and paid-job names.
I’d say **2028 thinking AI** reaches calls before robots.
think: I think AGI could take my **lead headset work**.
I see **under one month saved** as a near mortgage gap.
do: Defer the **usable kitchen table** replacement and put extra pay toward the next mortgage bill.
Seek **posted reception work** after 2028 with mortgage-covering wage and hours.
Take a **funded course** during paid time only if that posted paid reception role requires it.
S2.quote: The mortgage is due before a robot can enter our contact centre.
fieldNote: He knows **2028 thinking AI** is his work deadline.
The **table repair** protects cash for the mortgage.
Training requires a **posted paid job** and funded work hours.

steps.text: Delay replacing the usable kitchen table and keep the money for mortgage bills
Apply for posted paid reception work with written mortgage-covering wage and hours
Take funded course on paid time only if the posted reception job requires it

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives employers time to post real work and teach people while they still earn. I would ask which complaint posts are actually being filled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think five years could let me move from calls to written complaint review if a centre pays for the training. I still expect AGI could read and reason through those cases too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take a funded complaint-review course on paid time only if a posted paid vacancy requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that job only if its written wage and hours cover our mortgage, and keep paid calls if no review place opens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I can ask for a job posting before changing work. I would rather learn a real queue than pay for a title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you observe in review?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would sit with the reviewer on three disputed refunds and write down what authority they have to correct an account. If they can only pass a form onward, the job is not what I need.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Dina check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Dina (my partner) the whole week’s wage and the hours behind it. We cannot pay a mortgage with an impressive hourly rate for two shifts.

I’d support **paid teaching** while agents still work.
think: I think I could reach **written complaint review** in five years.
I know **AGI may reach** that work too.
do: Take **funded complaint-review training** on paid time only if a posted paid vacancy requires it.
Apply for **posted review work** after 2031 at written mortgage-covering wage and hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to keep good agents paid while they learn new work. I would ask the centre to show its staffing plan each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could keep leading calls and build savings over ten years, but full thinking AI may still do that job in 2036. Robots around 2039 do not change my first deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the afternoon calls and put a fixed amount from each pay into our mortgage reserve. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for a posted paid account role only if my call hours fall and its written wage and hours cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about today’s bills, less pressed by 2036. Ten years before AGI reaches my calls in 2036 does not pay the mortgage due next week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which yearly number would you track?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask how many paid lead hours the centre has each year. A plan that counts only handled chats could hide fewer paid people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their school unless Dina (my partner) and I had a signed offer and a manageable journey. A move for a vague opening could cost us the house.

I’d defend **paid learning time** for experienced agents who must shift into new work.

I know **2036 thinking AI** may still end my calls.
do: Keep **afternoon calls** and save from each pay.
Seek **posted paid account work** after 2036 if hours fall, only with written mortgage-covering wages and hours.
feel: **Anxious** about current bills, less pressed by 2036.

fieldNote: His **thin cushion** keeps the long case anxious.
He wants **paid lead hours** in yearly plans.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Cheap thinking AI could take the calls and dispute checks I am paid for, and our mortgage cannot survive a long gap. I would need written notice, a real posted paid job with mortgage-covering hours, and paid work-time training only if that job requires it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how an agent learns to find a missing payment. My first supervisor sat beside me through a wrong refund instead of handing me a list of links.

headlineQuote: My first supervisor sat beside me through a wrong refund instead of handing me a list of links.
portrait: At **43**, Yusuf is a top-skilled contact-centre lead with a two-year diploma and lower pay.
He and Dina support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with less than one month saved.
He avoids **AI tools** and checks payment records himself.
He wants **posted paid work** and practical teaching if calls disappear.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his calls and dispute checks before he can secure another wage.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, posted mortgage-covering work and paid required training would help.
